description.purpose: The night's watchdog (R-AG-1, GH #1229). It carries no schedule of its own: ./writer orders one one-shot named `nightly-dream` under a fixed id for the next `night_at_utc` with every episode it writes (`rearm`, so the rest of the day orders the same moment), and two seconds ahead when the hive's `clock_op` lane asks for the night now. It sends, it does not generate: event_id becomes the run id and fired_at becomes the window end — the two values that make a dream run identifiable and idempotent.
description.use_when: Inside the memory hive, always. It is not a tick: a day nobody wrote arms no night. ./writer is its only sender, over the hive's one inbound edge to it, so it accepts `add` and nothing else (GH #1229).
description.not_in_scope: No cron, and no op from outside: the hive's `clock_op` lane ends at ./writer, which refuses everything but the night's trigger. A night missed while the colony was down fires once on its next start (`catch_up`, the strike is `late`); either way no window is lost -- the next run's window starts at the last completed one.
description.emits_meaning: hop.event_id/fired_at are promoted to context.dream_run/dream_to by the edge and clock the whole run; the body is a plain trigger. A refused order leaves as `timer_op_error`; no edge carries it on, so it is a dead letter.
description.consumes_meaning: One `add` with `rearm` at a time, from ./writer: the one-shot `nightly-dream` (`at`, `emit_to` ../dream-glue, `catch_up`). Every other op is refused as `op_not_accepted`.
examples: an episode written at 14:12 UTC -> one order for 03:00 UTC the next day; every later episode that day -> the same order, nothing changes
